summary: Phase 5 Smart Inventory & Verified Aircraft Catalog — both backend and frontend tested. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_aircraft_catalog_smart.py (10 tests, 10/10 pass) covering GET /api/aircraft/booking-types (9 types), GET /api/aircraft/public/featured (safety_score + amenity_score + verification_badge enrichment, limit cap), POST /api/aircraft/compare (auth guard, min-2/max-4 validation, highlights best_safety/best_amenities/best_value, 404 on unknown ids, commission hidden from customer pricing), and POST /api/aircraft/create with new fields (engine_type, cruise_speed_kmh, max_range_km, max_altitude_ft, tcas, oxygen_kit, parachute_system, crew_configuration.pilot_count/copilot_required/cabin_crew_count) — with GET-persistence verification via /api/aircraft/my-fleet. Frontend: enhanced CreateAircraftForm renders all 5 tabbed sections (Basic Info, Technical Specs, Amenities, Safety, Crew & Pricing) with all new fields visible — but only on route /operator/aircraft-catalog. The /operator/fleet route still opens a LEGACY 8-field 'Add New Aircraft' dialog (FleetManagement.js) that ignores all new schema fields — an operator using the primary Fleet Management link will bypass the enhanced form entirely. AircraftComparison.js and both CustomerPriceBreakup.js files are orphaned — no import anywhere in /app/frontend/src.

minor.issue: best_value uses `min(..., key=lambda x: x['pricing']['hourly'] or float('inf'))` — if an aircraft has hourly_price=0 (Quote-only), Python treats 0 as falsy and swaps it to +inf, which is the intended fallback. Fine, but note that None/0/missing all collapse to the same 'skip' behavior; consider explicit `if hourly is None`.

Comparison accepts a raw JSON list (List[str]) as the whole body instead of a Pydantic model. Works, but yields unhelpful 422 messages and no schema in OpenAPI. Recommend wrapping in `class CompareRequest(BaseModel): aircraft_ids: List[str]`.

Returns operator_email in every card even for anonymous public callers. PII leak — every /public/featured card exposes the operator's email address. Consider projecting it out for the public endpoint or replacing with a masked operator_display_name.

ui_bugs.issue: Enhanced 5-section CreateAircraftForm is only reachable at /operator/aircraft-catalog. The primary sidebar link 'Fleet Management' still points to /operator/fleet which renders the LEGACY FleetManagement.js dialog with only 8 flat fields (manufacturer, model, aircraft_type string, year, registration, capacity, hourly_rate, base_location, enrollment_odometer). Operators using the main Fleet link will NEVER enter engine_type / TCAS / oxygen_kit / parachute / crew_configuration and thus create aircraft that can never earn a Verified badge or non-zero safety_score.

Component is exported but NOT imported/rendered anywhere in the app (grep across /app/frontend/src returns only its own file). The /api/aircraft/compare backend endpoint is functional but customers have no way to open the comparison UI. Wire it into CustomerDashboard or AircraftCatalog listing (multi-select + Compare button).

TWO files exist and BOTH export CustomerPriceBreakup: /app/frontend/src/components/pricing/PriceBreakup.js AND /app/frontend/src/components/booking/CustomerPriceBreakup.js. Neither is imported anywhere in the app (component is orphaned). Duplicate implementations will drift; consolidate to one and wire into the customer booking/quote flow.
Radix Dialog warns: 'Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}' — accessibility violation. Add DialogDescription or aria-describedby.

integration_issues.issue: Backend POST /api/aircraft/compare works end-to-end (verified with 3 seeded verified aircraft — returned proper highlights with best_safety/best_amenities/best_value ids matching comparison entries), but the frontend has no UI to invoke it. AircraftComparison component is defined but not routed/imported.

action_items: Decide fate of /operator/fleet legacy FleetManagement.js dialog. Either (a) replace it with the enhanced CreateAircraftForm from AircraftCatalog.js so /operator/fleet and /operator/aircraft-catalog surface the same form, or (b) remove the /fleet sidebar entry so operators always land on /aircraft-catalog. Current state means most operators will silently skip the new schema.
Wire AircraftComparison.js into a route/entry point (e.g. CustomerDashboard search results 'Compare (2)' floating button) — the backend /api/aircraft/compare works but is unreachable from the UI.

Consolidate the duplicate CustomerPriceBreakup implementations (booking/CustomerPriceBreakup.js and pricing/PriceBreakup.js export the same name) into a single file and import it in the customer quote/booking flow.
Remove operator_email from /api/aircraft/public/featured (PII leak on anonymous endpoint).
Wrap /api/aircraft/compare body in a Pydantic model for proper OpenAPI schema + validation errors.
Add DialogDescription / aria-describedby to CreateAircraftForm Dialog for a11y compliance.
critical_code_review_comments: aircraft_catalog_routes.compare_aircraft (line 1330): `best_value = min(..., key=lambda x: x['pricing']['hourly'] or float('inf'))` collapses hourly=None and hourly=0 to the same bucket. Explicit `hourly if hourly is not None else float('inf')` avoids surprising future 0-price test cases.

aircraft_catalog_routes.get_featured_aircraft: response includes operator_email for every card and hits no auth — exposes operator PII to anonymous scrapers on /api/aircraft/public/featured. Project it out or replace with an operator_display field.
aircraft_catalog_routes.compare_aircraft takes `aircraft_ids: List[str]` directly as body — no BaseModel wrapper, no OpenAPI schema. Wrap in a Pydantic request model.

Frontend: AircraftComparison.js (component defined line 130) and BOTH CustomerPriceBreakup.js files are exported but never imported. Dead code shipping to production, and the /api/aircraft/compare backend cannot be exercised by any real user flow.

Frontend: /operator/fleet still routes to the legacy FleetManagement.js dialog (only 8 fields) while /operator/aircraft-catalog routes to the new CreateAircraftForm (5 sections, 40+ fields). Two divergent creation flows for the same collection (`aircraft_catalog`) is a data-quality bomb — new aircraft created via /fleet will have no engine_type, tcas, oxygen_kit or crew_configuration and therefore no valid safety_score/amenity_score.
AircraftCatalog.js is 1171 lines and CreateAircraftForm alone is ~740 lines. Above the 700-line file-size guideline — split each section into its own component for maintainability.
Backend calculate_safety_score / calculate_amenity_score are duplicated call sites (public/featured + compare) — DRY: fine as-is, but ensure both call the same helper (they do).

success_rate.frontend: 60% — enhanced form works at /operator/aircraft-catalog, but AircraftComparison + CustomerPriceBreakup are orphaned and /operator/fleet still uses a legacy 8-field dialog

seed_data_creation: One TEST aircraft (VT-SMRT*) auto-cleaned via async DB delete in the test's cleanup step. Three seeded verified aircraft (Bell 407 VT-AYX, Airbus H145 VT-AYH, Cessna Citation XLS VT-AYJ) confirmed present in /api/aircraft/public/featured with premium_verified status.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend for Phase 5 Smart Inventory is 100% functional (booking-types=9, featured with scores, compare with highlights, create-with-new-fields all persist). The three critical follow-ups for the developer agent are: (1) unify /operator/fleet + /operator/aircraft-catalog behind the enhanced form, (2) wire AircraftComparison to a real entry point (e.g. checkbox multi-select on public search results), (3) delete/consolidate the two orphan CustomerPriceBreakup files and import the winner into the quote/booking flow. Re-test the frontend after these are wired.
rca_of_the_issue: The enhanced Smart Inventory form was correctly added to AircraftCatalog.js and mounted at /operator/aircraft-catalog, but OperatorDashboard.js still routes /operator/fleet to the pre-existing FleetManagement.js dialog. Both dialogs write to the same aircraft_catalog collection but the legacy one omits all new schema keys, so aircraft created there cannot be verified or scored. Additionally AircraftComparison.js and CustomerPriceBreakup.js were built to consume the new /api/aircraft/compare endpoint and hide-commission pricing respectively, but were never imported in any parent component — grep of the entire /app/frontend/src tree confirms 0 imports outside the components' own files. Net effect: backend features fully functional and 10/10 tests pass, but ~40% of the shipped frontend for this phase is unreachable to end users.
